subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Directional Control Valves: Routing Flow
description: A quick, practical guide to Directional Control Valves: Routing Flow.

hook.text: A directional valve decides where fluid goes. Shift the spool and oil flows to extend. Shift again to retract.

buildup.text: A spool inside the valve body has lands and grooves. Moving the spool connects or blocks different ports.

discovery.text: A 4/3 valve has four ports and three positions — extend, neutral, and retract. One valve controls the whole cylinder.

twist.text: The center position matters. Some center positions lock the cylinder. Others let it float free. Design chooses.

climax.text: Solenoid-operated directional valves respond to electrical signals. A computer now decides which way the fluid flows.

punchline.text: Move the spool. Redirect the river. Control the machine.

quiz.question: What does the center position of a 4/3 directional valve determine?
options: How fast the fluid flows through the valve in either direction
Whether the cylinder locks in place, floats, or slowly drifts when idle
The maximum pressure the valve can handle during operation
